A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same contextual-bandit framework for online fair division, despite retitling and reorganization. Their text, equations, figures, table, and complete appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v1 Section 5 reports original synthetic experiments comparing algorithms and examining agent count, feature dimension, and fairness-efficiency trade-offs.

after.justification: v2 Section 5 and Appendix D report original synthetic experiments, including copy-count sensitivity and revised nonlinear evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 corrects the Thompson-sampling distribution's mean from a scalar predicted utility to the estimated parameter vector. This changes the mathematical specification; the OFD allocation and update procedures otherwise remain the same.

E1.justification: v2 adds controlled repeated-item arrival scenarios with varying copies per item and revises the nonlinear synthetic instances. Coverage remains synthetic online allocation with linear and nonlinear utilities; no real-world dataset or application domain is added.

E2.justification: v1 Figure 1d compares OFD-GP-UCB/TS against linear OFD-UCB/TS. The replacement nonlinear comparison in v2 Figure 5 instead uses nOFD-Uniform and nOFD-Greedy against nOFD-UCB/TS. Baseline membership in the linear experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The nonlinear evaluation changes from a 500-round square-utility experiment at d=4 to 10,000-round polynomial-feature experiments at d=4,6,10,20. The new copy-count protocol uses 1000/c distinct items with c=10,25,50,100,200. Existing linear settings remain, although v2 inconsistently associates its rho=1 discussion with Figure 3.

E4.justification: v2 Figures 2d and 2h add sensitivity analysis testing how repeated copies affect regret. The earlier direct comparison of linear and GP estimators on nonlinear utilities disappears. Agent-count, dimension, and fairness-parameter analyses largely persist.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are repeated 20 times and report 95% confidence intervals. New curves and changed interval values do not introduce a different statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds copy-count results and replaces the square-utility GP results with four polynomial-feature comparisons showing substantial TS/UCB separation. Figure 3b also revises the TS agent-count curves, including the final ordering of N=5 and N=10. The linear benchmark and fairness-versus-rho plots are unchanged. The replaced nonlinear results do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: v2 Section 2 explicitly introduces item arrivals drawn from an unknown distribution nu, and Table 1 changes the Lin-UCB confidence expression from horizon T to round t. The three main regret bounds and their proof arguments are retained; Definition 2 is expressed in equivalent notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: contextual modeling of numerous items with few copies, goodness-based allocation, sublinear regret guarantees, and empirical validation. The new contribution list makes these existing claims explicit.

C2.justification: New Appendix B explains the per-round regret objective, offers a Markovian interpretation, and explains why the oracle excludes future observation noise. v2 also interprets increased item repetition as easing utility estimation. The future-work boundaries remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly reports an AMD EPYC 7543 server, 256GB RAM, and eight RTX 3080 GPUs. It also documents polynomial-feature construction and constant removal, although its degree-2 description conflicts with cubic terms in the example. These disclosures do not establish a hardware change.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of Bhattacharya et al. (2024), Schiffer and Zhang (2025), partial-information allocation, and Nash-regret research. It removes the blanket statement that fair-bandit work considers only fairness and drops the two references supporting the removed GP experiment. The central positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, substantially edits the introduction and explanatory prose, adds an explicit contribution list, and reorganizes related work and proof prerequisites. The supplement is restructured around related work, regret discussion, proofs, experiments, and auxiliary observations.

P2.justification: v2 adds an introductory schematic and combines retained linear and fairness plots with new copy-count plots into an eight-panel Figure 2. The rho=1 analysis moves to Appendix D, and a four-panel nonlinear figure replaces the earlier single panel. Legends and captions also change, with some incorrect cross-references.

improvement.justification: The copy-count analysis, TS formula correction, and added regret and hardware explanations provide benefits. However, the replacement nonlinear experiment describes degree-2 features using an example containing cubic terms, while the main discussion associates Figure 3 with the wrong rho setting. These inconsistencies affect interpretation and reproducibility of revised evidence, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
